newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs and pork bellies seen steady to higher.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs and pork bellies seen steady to higher.

text.p: CME hog futures were expected to open steady to 0.300 cent a lb higher while pork bellies were called steady to 0.250 higher, livestock analysts said.

Strength was seen in hog futures after values set new contract highs in October and December Friday. Further strength is expected to stem from expected steady to higher cash hog prices and a mostly bullish Cold Storage report Friday. Ham stock figures were bullish, especially bone-in stocks which were 66 percent of a year ago, analysts said.
The storage report showed good demand for pork products, which likely will continue, sources said.

The storage report was considered mostly neutral for pork belly futures but support was also expected as there were no surprises in the report and belly stocks were reported at comparably low levels. But the most supportive factor in pork bellies was the larger-then-expected slaughter last week and rising cash belly prices, they said.

However, scale-up technical resistance is again likely after prices failed to penetrate chart resistance near the 80.000 cent area last week. Bellies likely will be mostly a technically traded market until later in the year as usual for this time of year, analysts said.
